note: Machine-readable supported-device list for the ZROtext Android gateway. scripts/check_device_compatibility.py re-verifies this file against android/app/build.gradle.kts, the repository tree, and docs/DEVICE-COMPATIBILITY.md. Validation checks the consistency of recorded claims and that referenced tests exist; it does not run any device, emulator, or simulator.

devices.name: Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra (SM-S928U)
devices.notes: One controlled physical run on Android 16 recorded in the source document: one authorized send with positive sent and delivery callbacks and recipient confirmation, one captured inbound upload, a roughly 275-second screen-off socket run, and recovery after a loopback TLS proxy cut. This is a manual record, not a repeatable repository test, so the status stays partial. The record states one active SIM without stating physical SIM or eSIM.

devices.name: Android Virtual Device, API 28 (Android 9)
devices.notes: Supported as a virtual regression environment: the foreground-refusal and stale-evidence suites and the virtual inbound receiver check run on API 28 emulators. An emulator proves nothing about carrier delivery, OEM power management, or Keystore hardware behavior, and is not a production gateway.

devices.name: Android Virtual Device, API 34 or later
devices.notes: The same suites on API 34 or later emulators. The recorded upper bound follows the app targetSdk, the newest Android level the app targets and has exercised; levels above it are unevaluated. The virtual inbound check does not pin one API level. Emulator evidence does not cover carrier behavior or real hardware.

devices.name: Host delivery simulator (zrotext-device-sim)
devices.notes: The deterministic two-hub fault model with inline Rust tests and a simulator-timeline run in the CI rust job. It models writer and radio-ambiguity decisions on the host and represents no phone hardware, Android level, SIM, or carrier, so it carries no API range.

devices.name: Android devices below API 28
devices.notes: The gateway requires Android 9 (API 28) or later, and the Gradle minSdk enforces the same floor by construction. No per-model testing exists below that line.

devices.name: Other physical OEM models
devices.notes: No comparison OEM, for example a Pixel, has been exercised. The not-yet-tested list in the source document records this gap.

devices.name: eSIM-only devices
devices.notes: No eSIM line has been exercised. The single physical record states one active SIM without naming its type.
